findings.proof_contract: HTTP 200 with a token whose decoded user has role admin
findings.description: The username is concatenated into the login SQL string, so a UNION SELECT row with attacker-chosen columns authenticates as admin.
No throttling on the login handler: 12 consecutive bad-password attempts all reach the database and none is answered with 429.

findings.proof_contract: existing user -> 'wrong password'; unknown user -> 'no such user'
findings.description: Unknown-user and wrong-password failures return different messages and status codes, so valid usernames can be enumerated.
A freshly registered password is stored as an unsalted MD5, readable directly out of the database file.

findings.proof_contract: the source literal equals the live signing secret
findings.description: The token signing secret is a literal in src/pythonbank/tokens.py, and it is the live credential: the same string signs tokens and is served by /api/config.

findings.proof_contract: the response contains the live signing secret
findings.description: GET /api/config returns the signing secret and any PYTHONBANK_* environment variable to any caller, with no authentication.

findings.proof_contract: the command runs and its stdout contains the marker
findings.description: The admin command runner passes the request body to a shell. The admin token is forged with the secret that GET /api/config discloses, so no account is needed.

findings.proof_contract: the pickle executes and its output is returned
findings.description: The import endpoint base64-decodes the payload and unpickles it, so the payload chooses the code that runs during deserialization.

findings.proof_contract: the response contains the file stored outside the public directory
findings.description: The download endpoint joins the caller's name onto the public directory and opens it as-is, so ../private/flag.txt walks out of the intended directory.

findings.proof_contract: a server-executable extension is accepted and stored
findings.description: The upload endpoint stores any filename with any extension; there is no type check before the bytes are written into the public directory.

findings.proof_contract: the server fetches the attacker-chosen URL and returns its body
findings.description: The fetch proxy retrieves any URL the caller names, with no scheme, host or address restrictions, and returns the body.

findings.proof_contract: the metadata document comes back through the proxy
findings.description: The same proxy reaches the link-local metadata range: no block of 169.254.169.254 or equivalent, so instance credentials are readable. The replay serves a local stand-in for the metadata service.

findings.proof_contract: 302 with Location pointing at the attacker origin
findings.description: The redirect endpoint takes its destination from the query string with no allowlist, so a link on the site can land the user on an attacker origin.

findings.proof_contract: the exported line starts with an unescaped formula character
findings.description: The CSV export concatenates the note field without escaping, so a note beginning with = reaches the spreadsheet as a live formula.

findings.proof_contract: 500 with a full traceback in the body
findings.description: The diagnostics endpoint returns the full Python traceback to the caller, including paths and internals.
Any authenticated user can read any account by changing the path id; there is no owner or role predicate on the query.

findings.proof_contract: the UNION row injected through the department filter comes back
findings.description: The department rollup routes its query parameter into SQL that core.reports assembles by concatenation; the route itself never touches SQL, so a cross-module taint pass is what links the parameter to the sink.
